distractors.reason: 'Highly' is used with adjectives like 'highly recommended' or 'highly unlikely'. We don't say 'highly good' in everyday English.
'Deeply' goes with feelings and states like 'deeply sad' or 'deeply concerned'. We don't say 'deeply good'.
'Fully' means completely, as in 'fully ready' or 'fully aware'. We don't say 'fully good' to mean something is very good.

l1_interference: Los hispanohablantes pueden traducir 'altamente' como 'highly' y decir 'highly good'. En inglés, para expresar un grado alto con 'good' se usa 'very good'.
explanation: 'Very' is the most general degree adverb and works with many common adjectives, such as 'very good', 'very big', and 'very nice'. 'Highly', 'deeply', and 'fully' are more specific and go only with certain adjectives.
memory_tip: VERY + good/big/nice (everyday adjectives) | HIGHLY + recommended/unlikely (formal) | DEEPLY + sad/concerned (strong emotion)
